doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: How the music was learned then versus in schools now
summary: Learning by watching and listening, with no jazz classes or books then.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I love hearing this and it makes me think about the learning process back then and how it gets passed on. You know Rick passed on that kind of thing to me, and I didn’t even have to ask for it. It was just like you said, watching and listening.
It’s so different from how most, now we go to universities to get it.

Yeah absolutely. You’re right, you’re right. And there’s some great, great schools and there are great programs now, music programs that we didn’t have. We didn’t have access to it. Rick, I don’t know, you know well I mean I’m older than you so, but I don’t remember jazz classes and stuff like that.
Like it is now, man. You know.
I think there was a book called Bugs Bower.
There was. I remember that name.
And that was the only like information. Like what a God, you know.
And it was, yeah, valuable, at the time.
